newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends down, gilt yields flat.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends down, gilt yields flat.

text.p: Indian call money eased in closing trade on Tuesday to the 10.60-10.75 percent range, down from the day's high of 10.90 percent, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was done between 10.80 and 10.90 percent, they said.
Dealers said call money remained range bound on Tuesday in the absence of any market-moving factors.
"Market participants are waiting to see whether there is any cut in cash reserve requirements," a dealer said.

There were strong rumours in the market that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would announce a 50 basis point cut in cash reserve requirements in its credit policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March), due to announced in the first week of October, he said.
Dealers said secondary market prices of government securities prices remained steady in moderate trade.

"There is little position-taking at the moment," a dealer said. "As long as call remains at current levels, the market will remain subdued." Most of the current activity was on account of some market participants switching securities, he said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Tuesday at a yield of 13.15 percent against Monday's 13.14 percent, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.44 percent against 13.47 percent while the 13.62 percent 1998 was traded at 13.55 percent against 13.57 percent, they said.
Dealers reported little activity in certificates of deposit and commercial paper.
